scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9018: Hello, my connection from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) keeps going up and down -- works for a bit, drops, comes back,
over and over. The person who sits near the racks reckons "one of the
switches keeps restarting itself" (they mentioned a name like
leaf_router_0_0?) and thinks it should be swapped out, but I can't verify any
of that. Could someone please check what keeps going up and down and make it
stay up? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user reported intermittent loss between pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2), with anecdotal suspicion that leaf_router_0_0 was repeatedly restarting. A complete multi-layer diagnostic sweep of this dc_clos_bgp topology found no fault at any layer.

**Affected component:** None identified. No subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy is misconfigured or degraded.

**Mechanism (why there is no confirmed fault):** The intermittent-fault claim was ruled out by the absence of any causal mechanism and any historical trace — not merely by a single clean snapshot. Specifically: (1) all interface carrier counters on leaf_router_0_0 (eth0/eth1/eth2) show zero carrier changes since startup; (2) the BGP session history on leaf_router_0_0 shows exactly one session established and zero dropped, with zero NOTIFICATION messages exchanged; (3) FRR logs contain only normal 60-second KEEPALIVE traffic after the startup burst, with no NOTIFICATION, reset, or FSM error entries; (4) no flap script, cron job, or stress process exists on any device in the lab.

**Localization:** leaf_router_0_0 specifically — and all five BGP routers, both hosts, all 16 interfaces — are healthy. L2 identity (no duplicate MACs), ACL/firewall (no drop rules), traffic control (default fq_codel, no shaping), and BGP control plane (all 5 peers Established) are all clean.

**Root cause:** There is no current or historically traceable fault — the "keeps going up and down" complaint is unconfirmed and cannot be attributed to any mechanism present in the lab.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The topology is operating normally. If the symptom recurs, collect packet captures or interface counters in real time to obtain direct evidence of the fault.
